did.abstract: The Jeffrey Lewis papers contain his screenwriter and producer work for the television series Hill Street Blues , and as a novelist on his first book series the Meritocracy Quartet which consists of Meritocracy: A Love Story, Conference of the Birds, Theme Song for an Old Show, and Adam the King.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: Jeffrey Lewis born in New York City on July 4, 1944, to Richard Lewis and Alice Lisson. He attended Yale University receiving a Bachelor of Arts in 1966, and a Doctor of Law (JD) from Harvard University in 1970. Early in his career he was an assistant district attorney and criminal defense lawyer in Manhattan and worked for a short time with Stan Lee at Marvel. His father, Richard Lewis, was an executive producer of classic American TV and radio of the golden age.

An American novelist, television screenwriter and producer, Lewis has published eight novels to date. The Meritocracy Quartet, Meritocracy: A Love Story, Conference of the Birds, Song for an Old Show, and Adam the King ; his other novels are Berlin Cantata, The Inquisitor's Diary, Bealport: A Novel of a Town. Land of Cockaigne, and Leonard Cohen.

Lewis was a producer and screen writer for the 1980s seven-season television series Hill Street Blues , winning two Emmys with twelve nominations, and a Writers Guild of America Award. For the final season of Hill Street Blues Lewis brought on David Milch, his former Yale roommate, as co-show runner. Some individual episodes of this season had writing contributions by prominent guest writers such as David Mamet and Bob Woodward.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Jeffrey Lewis papers contain his screenwriting and producing work for the television series, Hill Street Blues , and as a novelist on his first series the Meritocracy Quartet which consists of Meritocracy: A Love Story , Conference of the Birds , Theme Song for an Old Show , and Adam the King . The collection contains notes, ideas, and scripts for, Hill Street Blues and notes, ideas, drafts, and promotional material for his four novels with a small amount of correspondences correlated to the end of his second novel in the series, Conference of the Birds , which includes a correspondence with the author giving context about his papers and writing overall for both the television and book series.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The Jeffrey Lewis papers consists of two series. The first series is for the television series Hill Street Blues divided into two sub-series by season and episodes. The first sub-series is chronological with story ideas, notes, newspaper clippings, and partial script runs. The second sub-series is chronological with finished scripts organized by season and episode.

The second series is divided into four sub-series for each book in the Meritocracy Quartet novels. Each sub-series is organized chronologically by notes and ideas, drafts, correspondence and promotional material for each novel, Meritocrary: A Love Story, Conference of the Birds, Theme Song for an Old Show and Adam the King .

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: These materials have been arranged and described according to national and local standards. For more information, please refer to the Yale Archival Processing Manual.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: This series is arranged chronologically by season and episodes into two sub-series. The first subseries contains ideas, notes, rough drafts of parts of scripts. The second subseries is finished scripts.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains material related to the television series Hill Street Blues divided into two sub-series. The first is story ideas, notes, and partial drafts, the second is finished scripts.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: This series is arranged in chronogical order of the four books in the Meritocrary Quartet each as subseries. Each subseries begins with conception ideas, notes, and drafts followed by completed drafts of each novel. There are some correspondence following the final draft of The Conference of the Birds .

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series is the Meritocracy Quartet. Four separate novels set in the author's experiences in the decades of the 1960s, 1970s, 1980s, and 1990s.
